display.title: Shin-Dalet-Yud: How the Mezuzah Guards Our Homes
display.summary_short: Why the letters Shin-Dalet-Yud on the back of the mezuzah face out, what they stand for, and how Hashem guards us at home and on the way.
display.summary_long: A Mitzvah Time lesson from the Tzivos Hashem radio show. Uncle Yossi explains that when the mezuzah is rolled into its case, the three letters Shin, Dalet, Yud written on its back should face out, at the top. Together they form one of Hashem's holy Names, which we say only while davening or learning a full verse. The Sages teach that the letters also stand for 'Shomer Dalsos Yisroel', the Guardian of the doors of Israel: Shin for shomer, guardian; Dalet for dalsos, doors; Yud for Yisroel. Some say the Dalet also stands for diros, dwellings, because Hashem protects the whole house and everyone in it. The mezuzah's protection continues as we leave home until we return, so it is good to say 'Hashem yishmor tzeisi u'vo'i', Hashem will guard my going out and coming in. Every glance at the mezuzah reminds us that Hashem is welcome in our home, that everything in it belongs to Him, and that He watches over us, which is why we lovingly touch and kiss it.
display.lesson: The mezuzah reminds us that Hashem guards our home and everyone in it, so greet it with love.
